newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end lower, shrug off Wall St bulls.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end lower, shrug off Wall St bulls.

text.p: The CAC 40 index closed lower on Tuesday in relatively light volume as investors took their cue from uncertainty over the euro to book profits.
Traders said the market needed to consolidate after the surprise rise since the Socialist election win. The bourse shrugged off Wall Street's attack on the 7,500 level and London's record high.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 22.02 points or 0.82 percent at 2,664.18. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 21 at 2,647 from Monday's close.
The franc's weaker tone, on the back of Monday's row over the stability pact, caused some concern, traders said. The Franco-German summit on Friday at Poitiers, central France, may give some relief.
"The dissensions between France and Germany on the stability pact are weighing," one trader said.
French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's planned speech to the National Assembly on June 19 is also expected to clarify the Socialist government's policy.
Eurotunnel gained 3.82 percent to 6.80 francs, on shareholder groups' efforts to get a sweeter deal from banks.
A Paris investigating magistrate told Reuters she will go to London later this month as part of her probe into alleged insider trading in Eurotunnel shares.
Legrand ended up 3.35 percent at 1,050, bouncing from Monday's fall. The company gave a presentation to a brokerage Tuesday morning.
Pernod Ricard advanced 3.05 percent at 300.8 francs, helped by its deal with fast food chain MacDonald for the distribution of its Orangina drink in France.
Renault dropped 4.63 percent to 127.80 francs. The carmaker will commission an independent study to consider alternatives to closing its Vilvoorde plant.
